profile.campus: DATA4 MAD02 Campus, San Agustín del Guadalix, Madrid
profile.address: San Agustín del Guadalix, 28750 Madrid, Spain
profile.reading:
DC02 is the second numbered building on DATA4's newer MAD02 campus at San Agustín del Guadalix, a town north of Madrid, Spain, distinct from the operator's established MAD01 campus in nearby Alcobendas. DATA4, the French headquartered developer and operator behind both campuses, announced the San Agustín del Guadalix campus on April 27, 2023 and broke ground that May, describing a design target of four buildings, 16,000 square meters of IT space, and 80 megawatts of total capacity, an average of 20 megawatts per building by trade press arithmetic though DATA4 did not publish a per-building split itself. The project carried a reported 530 million euro price tag, part of an 850 million euro DATA4 investment program across Spain running through 2030, with a first phase originally targeted for 2025 and full build out originally targeted for 2029. DATA4's Spain country director framed MAD02 as oriented more toward hyperscale cloud tenants than the colocation focused MAD01 campus.

DC02 reached BREEAM Excellent Design Stage certification on September 2, 2025, trade coverage's first report of that certification tier at a Spanish DATA4 site, built around heat recovery for nearby residential heating, rainwater and greywater recycling, low emission concrete, recycled materials in paving and cladding, and onsite photovoltaic generation. As of that September 2025 certification, DC02 was still described as under construction. A separate March 2026 report said the first of the campus's four planned buildings had begun operating with a closed loop, water free cooling system, without specifying whether the activated building was DC01 or DC02. Since DATA4's own Spain leadership had originally targeted DC01, not DC02, for a 2025 start of operations, and DC02 was reported under construction as recently as September 2025, the more likely reading is that the building activated in March 2026 was DC01, and DC02's operational start had not been confirmed as of this research.

A Comunidad de Madrid gazette filing from July 2025, under the name DATA4 Castilla, S.L., sought a municipal license for a generation plant to power a data center on Parcel P3 of the SAU-8 Los Ardales industrial estate, the estate hosting the MAD02 campus, and named DC01 specifically. A separate March 2026 regional transparency filing by DATA4 Infrastructure Spain, S.L.U. sought temporary rights to cross six historic livestock droving routes across four municipalities, Algete, Fuente el Saz de Jarama, El Molar, and San Agustín de Guadalix, to install an underground 66 kilovolt high voltage connection feeding a data center under construction at SAU-8 Los Ardales, without naming a specific building.

DATA4's own current Madrid landing page treats MAD02 as a 50 megawatt campus across 6.7 hectares, part of a 100 megawatt, two site Madrid total together with MAD01. That figure is smaller than, and harder to reconcile with, the 2023 announcement's four building, 80 megawatt design target, and likely reflects capacity commissioned to date rather than the finished design. No building specific megawatt, utility interconnection, standby generation, or onsite generation figure for DC02 itself was found in any operator or regulatory source reviewed, so none of the four power figures is recorded for this specific building. DATA4's ownership moved from AXA Investment Managers Alternatives to Brookfield Infrastructure in a deal completed August 2023 for 2.4 billion dollars, and in August 2025 Brookfield brought in Arjun Infrastructure Partners and Interogo Holding as new shareholders in a stake sale covering a stabilised, 244 megawatt DATA4 portfolio spanning Paris, Milan, and Madrid, valued at 3.6 billion dollars per a Brookfield SEC filing. Because MAD02 was still under construction as recently as September 2025, it is unclear whether this building falls inside that stabilised, already income producing pool the 2025 sale describes, or remains a newer asset built too recently to qualify. No tenant name for DC02 was found in any source reviewed.

profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-05: prior version cited a banned aggregator for the DC02 12.5 MW figure. That figure is dropped, it_capacity_mw removed, since no operator or regulatory source found this session confirms a building-specific MW figure for DC02. Found instead: a July 2025 BOCM municipal license filing (DATA4 Castilla S.L., DC01, SAU-8 Los Ardales, generation plant) and a March 2026 Comunidad de Madrid transparency filing (DATA4 Infrastructure Spain S.L.U., 66kV underground line, six vías pecuarias crossed) as genuine regulatory primary sources, plus a Sept 2025 BREEAM Excellent Design Stage certification for DC02 specifically (still under construction at that date) and a March 2026 report of the first of four buildings activating, most likely DC01 given the construction status reported five months earlier. Corporate ownership extended to the August 2025 Arjun Infrastructure Partners / Interogo Holding stake sale. Sibling rows (MAD2-DC01 way/1471932562, generic MAD2 Campus way/1471935097) still carry older sourcing as of this write and were not in this session scope for full rewrite. [session addition 2026-09-06] campus_power_note updated to add the March 2026 activation report's "70 to 80 MW" campus phrasing, keeping this field identical in substance to the version now on sibling row MAD2-DC01 (osm:way/1471932562), which was updated in the same session for internal consistency across the MAD02 building set.
profile.campus_power_note: The four power numbers for DATA4's MAD02 campus need to stay separate because two campus wide totals are in circulation and no building specific figure survives this research. DATA4's own current Madrid page states the MAD02 campus is 50 megawatts across 6.7 hectares, part of a 100 megawatt combined Madrid total with MAD01. The operator's April 2023 announcement instead described a four building design target of 16,000 square meters of IT space and 80 megawatts once complete. A March 2026 trade press report on the first building's activation described the campus target loosely as 70 to 80 megawatts across four buildings, another variant of the same design figure. Both totals are campus wide capacity or design figures, not utility interconnection ratings, standby generator ratings, or onsite generation figures, none of which were found published for this campus. A July 2025 Comunidad de Madrid municipal license filing for a generation plant to power DC01, and a March 2026 regional filing for a 66 kilovolt underground connection into the SAU-8 Los Ardales estate, confirm real grid and backup infrastructure work underway, but neither filing discloses a megawatt rating. This registry records the 50 MW / 6.7 ha figure as the operator's current simplified marketing number and the 80 MW / four building figure as the design end state, without resolving the gap, and attributes no building specific figure to any single building on this campus.
